topic: FLIP floating laboratory and ocean measurement
centralQuestion: Why would scientists intentionally tip a floating laboratory upright?
thesis: Controlled rotation changed the platform geometry to reduce wave response and improve a scientific reference, without eliminating ocean motion.
viewerPayoff: Understand why an extraordinary-looking laboratory was shaped to distinguish ocean behavior from instrument motion.

caveats.statement: Historical original design. Reduced motion is not immobility; deep-water surface-wave attenuation varies with wavelength. Controlled ballast sequence and hull diagram are simplified, not an engineering operating procedure. No universal motion ratio, literal still-water depth, invented data trace or current-service claim.

hooks.text: Scientists deliberately tipped this floating laboratory upright. Why?
hooks.viewerPromise: Resolve the deliberate rotation through ballast, hull geometry and scientific measurement.

hooks.text: How do you measure a moving ocean from a moving laboratory?
hooks.viewerPromise: See the platform itself become part of the measurement solution.
